name: Q4 Joint-Switch Equality-Partition Counterexample
definition: On the vertices $0,\ldots,15$ of $Q_4$, orient edges forward in the corner-peeling orders $\alpha=(9,1,11,10,14,15,13,3,12,7,2,6,8,5,0,4)$ and $\gamma=(11,3,15,2,13,10,7,5,14,9,8,12,6,1,0,4)$. For a bit assignment $s$ on the vertices, augment the first orientation by $x\to z$ whenever $x\to y$ is a crossing edge for $s$ and $z$ is a descendant of $y$ in the second orientation.
properties: Individually incompatible crossings force seven equality blocks: $\{0\}$, $\{1,3,5,7\}$, $\{4\}$, $\{6\}$, $\{2,10\}$, $\{9,11,13,14,15\}$, and $\{8,12\}$. Among their 128 assignments, exactly 96 give an acyclic augmented graph. Feasibility is the disjunction that the block $\{1,3,5,7\}$ agrees with $\{2,10\}$ or with $\{9,11,13,14,15\}$. The indicators of the last two blocks are feasible separately, while their sum is infeasible despite every crossing being individually compatible.
